item.title: MP opposes potential service cuts at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
MP opposes potential service cuts at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
North West Norfolk MP James Wild has voiced strong opposition to reports suggesting a potential downgrade of A&E, intensive care, and maternity services at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. Mr Wild met with the chief executive of the Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group to express concerns over a lack of transparency regarding a working group currently reviewing long-term service strategies.
The MP argued that removing consultant-led services would be unacceptable for rural communities, citing the impact on ambulance travel times and patient access. A review is expected to report to the hospital group’s board in October. Mr Wild has received assurances that the current review will not jeopardise plans for a new hospital facility.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/answer-to-qeh-s-challenges-is-to-improve-care-not-remove-s-9482091/

item.title: Former King’s Lynn hospital nurse struck off
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Former King’s Lynn hospital nurse struck off
A former nurse at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has been removed from the nursing register. Adam Feary was previously convicted of possessing over 14,000 indecent images of children and animals, as well as a manual encouraging sexual offending.
The Nursing and Midwifery Council’s Fitness to Practise Committee concluded that Feary’s actions breached fundamental professional standards. While he received a suspended prison sentence last year, the committee determined that an immediate interim order was necessary to protect the public. Feary, who worked at the hospital until July 2023, has been placed on the sex offenders register for ten years. The Queen Elizabeth Hospital confirmed his employment was terminated following an internal investigation.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/former-qeh-nurse-struck-off-after-being-found-with-nearly-14-9482463/

Free weekly running sessions offered at Wisbech Park
Residents across the Fens are being invited to join a free, weekly running programme at Wisbech Park. Organised by Active Fenland, the Couch to 5k sessions take place every Tuesday morning between 9:30am and 10:30am.
The group is led by England Athletics-qualified coach Gary Bligh and is open to all abilities, regardless of previous running experience. Organisers say the sessions focus on building confidence and stamina in a supportive environment, with no pressure to meet specific pace targets. Beyond the physical exercise, the group offers a social opportunity for participants to meet new people. Those interested in taking part can simply turn up to the park to get involved.

item.title: Petition launched to protect services at King’s Lynn hospital
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Petition launched to protect services at King’s Lynn hospital
A petition to save key departments at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has reached 7,000 signatures. Residents are concerned about reports that the hospital’s Accident and Emergency, intensive care, and maternity units could face a downgrade.
Local politicians are seeking urgent meetings with the Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group to demand clarity. While the hospital group insists that no decisions have been made regarding future service configurations, they are currently developing a long-term clinical strategy for the region. A spokesperson confirmed that any potential changes would require public consultation. The hospital is set to discuss its future at an annual members’ meeting this Thursday, which is open to the public.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/thousands-sign-petition-to-save-services-at-qeh-as-politic-9482257/
